newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bulls advance as Germany's DAX index hits records.
newsitem.headline: Bulls advance as Germany's DAX index hits records.

text.p: Chartists say bulls are in the ascendant in Germany as the DAX index surged to record highs in bourse trade on Tuesday, gaining four percent in the last four weeks, and with sights set on 2,850 points for the year-end.
The DAX index ended bourse trade 1.28 percent higher at 2,728.45 points, a gain of 34.57 points, and technical analysts said there was still room for the market to go higher.
The bull run has been mainly driven by strong performances on the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street, always closely monitored by German share traders, and the ongoing strength of the dollar.

The extent of recent gains took most chartists by surprise. Both bulls and bears agree that the market is overbought at the moment, and feel a correction is probably due at some stage. But the timing and extent of a correction is a contentious issue among technical analysts.

"We were surprised by the extent of the advance on the market, and I would say we weren't the only ones. We can see the market hitting 2,750 points before the end of the week," said Marcel Mussler, chartist at DG Bank in Frankfurt.
Mussler said that DG Bank is leaving its year-end forecast for the DAX at 2,850 points,

"We had been expecting a correction down to 2,650, but this no longer looks likely as market sentiment indicators are now neutral in the mid-term and I think we are a good distance away from a mid-term sell signal," said Volker Bien, chartist at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.

"I would say that even the 2,780-point level isn't too high a forecast at the moment and frequency density indicators are pointing to strong support for the index at 2,570. There is strong market acceptance between 2,530 and 2,570 points," said Bien.
Bien said another big factor behind the gains was a surge of interest in the German automobile sector, which had been a somewhat sleepy segment until now.
Mussler agrees: "There are buy signals in Daimler AG and BMW AG, while utilities and chemicals are also looking very good technically."
Mussler was less positive on the banking, insurance, construction and retail sectors, but insisted that he was not pessimistic and that all sectors were putting in a good performance at the moment.
On the trading floor, some dealers who closely follow technical indicators remain sceptical of the significance of the market's recent rally.
Paul Lewis, proprietary trader at BNP in Frankfurt, said volatility in the options market has increased.
"In options bidding the volatility is up, and normally the volatility is bid down in a rally. This could be because the anniversary of the stock market crash in 1987 is coming up," said Lewis.

I do think that when the correction comes it's going to be short and it's going to be sharp. This market is massively overbought. As to where we'll be at the end of the year -- that's pot luck," said Lewis.
Lewis said according to Fibonacci numbers a correction to 2,683 points makes sense, possibly this week.

"The only people telling you to buy this market are the momentum traders and of course they are right when the market is going up. But they are also very exposed if things turn around on the DAX," said Lewis.
